 A chilly, breezy start to the week; dangerous rip currents at the beaches 
 By Matt Barrentine Updated : 19 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google MOBILE, Ala. ( WALA ) - Clouds and scattered showers are moving across the Gulf Coast this morning, and more rain is making it to the ground earlier than originally expected. Some of the lighter returns are still evaporating before reaching the surface, but we’re seeing enough showers reach the ground to produce some wet roads and occasional light rainfall. Rain should remain generally light and spotty, with no significant rainfall expected.
 Temperatures are starting off cool, and a northeast breeze will keep things feeling more like late fall today. Highs will struggle to reach 60 degrees in many locations.
 Monday: Mostly cloudy, cool and breezy, with scattered light showers possible through the morning. While some rain will evaporate before reaching the ground, other showers will produce measurable rainfall. Highs will be near 60, with northeast winds around 10 to 15 mph. Tonight stays mostly cloudy, with lows in the upper 40s to around 50 near the coast.
 Tuesday: A gradual improvement begins. Clouds will break at times, and temperatures rebound into the upper 60s. Rain chances become very low, with a cool start to the day.
 Wednesday and Thursday: Warmer weather returns, with a good deal of sunshine. Highs should climb into the middle 70s, with overnight lows moderating into the upper 50s and lower 60s. The overall pattern remains mostly dry.
 Friday and the weekend: Temperatures should stay mild, with highs in the middle to upper 70s. Clouds may increase at times, and there is some uncertainty about a possible disturbance approaching late in the weekend. For now, rain chances look limited, but we’ll keep an eye on that trend.
 Beach and boating conditions: This is the big concern this week. A High Rip Current Risk is in effect for Alabama beaches beginning this evening through late Thursday night. The high risk begins Tuesday morning for the western Florida Panhandle beaches and continues through late Thursday night. Surf is expected to build from 3 to 4 feet today to around 4 to 6 feet Tuesday, with strong easterly winds continuing. A Small Craft Advisory is also in effect for Gulf waters, with seas building to 5 to 8 feet. This is not a good stretch for swimming or taking smaller boats into the Gulf. Stay out of the water when the high risk is in effect, and check the latest beach and marine forecasts before heading out.
